questions.prompt: Minimum opening raise in a no-limit game is generally…

choices.text: A raise to at least two big blinds.
Any amount above the big blind, even one dollar.
The size of the pot only.

questions.explanation: An open must at least double the big blind, unless the house posts otherwise.

choices.text: Passing when there is no bet.
A call of zero that closes the hand.
Only legal in the big blind preflop.

questions.explanation: Check means 'no bet' and keeps your cards live.

questions.prompt: You say 'call' and then try to raise after seeing a frown. That raise…

choices.text: Is a legal string if chips remain.
Is too late; the call stands.

questions.explanation: The declaration bound you. Changing it is not a strategy, it is a rules problem.

questions.prompt: All-in for less than the pot on the river…

choices.text: Is a legal bet for the chips you have; opponents may call that amount.

questions.explanation: You may go all-in for whatever you have left. They call the lesser amount.
